newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hope for China WTO accord by fall - U.S.'s Sasser.
newsitem.headline: Hope for China WTO accord by fall - U.S.'s Sasser.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to China James Sasser said on Friday there was hope talks on China's World Trade Organisation (WTO) entry could be concluded in time for President Jiang Zemin's visit to Washington this autumn.

Sasser told a business luncheon in Hong Kong that the U.S. administration would continue to push vigorously to try to effect a WTO agreement with China in conjunction with other members of the global trade body.

"There is hope that could be concluded in time when President Jiang Zemin visits this fall to the United States," Sasser said. "I think there is hope. Realistically, it's going to be difficult to do, but not impossible."

Jiang is expected to visit the United States later this year for a proposed summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton. Talks on preparations for the meeting are expected when Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen visits Washington next week.
China's entry into the WTO has long been delayed as members urged Beijing to improve market access and further create a level playing filed.
